texts: good. the proposal, the experiment and the three-source group with its count all land, and the experiment symbol is reused when the Council approves it. One caveat no rewrite can fix: our calendar terms offer only a day-of-month slot, so 'day 425' is stored there — the number survives but the slot does not mean day-of-year, and we have filed that as a gap on our side.
good. the Council is one collective referent and the approval attaches to the very experiment symbol introduced in the previous sentence.

good. the filling, the sea-water as what it was filled with, and its origin in the named tide-pools all come through, with sea-water linked to water and the Tide-pools also typed as a pool from the kind word inside the name.
good. same shape as the Cauldron One fill, with a second, distinct batch of sea-water and 'deep' kept as a property of the ebb rather than fused into a kind name.
good. harbor water is typed as a kind of water, and its origin is the middle, which is held as a part of the pier.
good. one boiling event over a thread group, located in a three-member cauldron group that is linked back to Cauldron One, Two and Three by name, with the one-day duration recorded as a measure.
good. the forming event places a fresh mire-essence witness in Cauldron One, with mire-essence linked to essence.

good. the yield reuses the very mire-essence that formed in that cauldron, and 'one vessel' is recorded as a quantity measure on it — we have no dedicated form for a container of-phrase, but nothing of the sentence is lost.
good. Cauldron Two gets its own mire-essence witness and its own forming event, correctly kept distinct from Cauldron One's.
good. the same yield-plus-quantity shape as Cauldron One's, on the second batch's own symbols.
good. the whole forming claim is denied as one bundle with the mire-essence witness held inside it, so nothing in the parse asserts that any mire-essence existed in Cauldron Three.
good. the residue gets its own witness with 'chalky' as a property of it, yielded by Cauldron Three.
good. the results are one definite group, and the Council is recognized as the same body that approved the experiment earlier.
good. the recording reuses the same results group, the ledger is kept as its own referent, and the results are treated as unaltered by being recorded, which is right.
